question: Where does the crackle in WASAPI exclusive come from?
statement: The bursts are created in the exclusive-mode path after the engine's output buffer (playback driver / card, analog loop, or exclusive capture), not by the program's own tone generation or mixing.
prediction: In every damaged capture the engine output.wav stays a clean tone while raw.wav shows bursts; shared and MME stay clean on the same cable.
refuted_if: A damaged raw.wav comes with a damaged output.wav, or the same cable and settings give bursts in shared mode.

question: Where does the crackle in WASAPI exclusive come from?
statement: The bursts come from the program's own stream handling in exclusive mode (PortAudio exclusive format conversion, stream arguments, 1-channel open of a stereo Line In), a software fault that a minimal PortAudio script would not show.
prediction: A minimal record-and-play script without the app, same device, API, rate and block, gives clean tone captures where the app gives bursts.
refuted_if: The minimal script shows the same bursts at the same setting (then the fault is below the app: driver or device).

question: Is any exclusive setting reliably clean, and what decides it?
statement: Exclusive-mode crackle is intermittent and decided by a state that can change between runs (stream open, mount age, device format, driver), so one clean capture proves little.
prediction: Repeated mount / capture / unmount at one block size gives a mixture of clean and damaged captures; burst rate within one capture stays constant; the exclusive 256 captures show no clean run in n >= 10 or some clean ones.
refuted_if: Ten or more identical repeats at one setting all give the same result (all clean or all damaged).

question: Is any exclusive setting reliably clean, and what decides it?
statement: Windows / driver settings of the onboard Realtek (24 bit device format and its conversion, exclusive-priority option, enhancements, Realtek vs Microsoft HD Audio driver, power plan) change how often the bursts occur.
prediction: Changing exactly one of these settings changes the bursts per second or the share of clean captures in exclusive 256 (3 captures per setting).
refuted_if: Each tested setting gives the same result as the baseline within the repeat spread.

question: What is the lowest real round trip per audio path, and can it be 20 ms or less?
statement: Some path on this PC (WASAPI exclusive, ASIO4ALL, WDM-KS) measures a round trip of 20 ms or less at a block size that is also free of crackle; the onboard Realtek can reach the goal.
prediction: latency_lab round trip median <= 20 ms in at least one path, and 3 clean 20 s Lab captures (under 1 % damaged windows, no all-zero blocks, underflows 0) at that setting.
refuted_if: Every path with a clean capture measures more than 20 ms, and every path at 20 ms or less gives damaged captures, in at least 3 captures each (then the goal needs other hardware).

question: What is the lowest real round trip per audio path, and can it be 20 ms or less?
statement: WASAPI shared and MME, the only paths measured clean so far, are slower than 20 ms round trip on this PC (the app text says about 37 ms for shared), so the goal cannot be reached in them.
prediction: latency_lab round trip for shared and MME at blocks 128 and 256 is above 20 ms in 3 calibrations each.
refuted_if: Shared or MME measures 20 ms or less in 3 calibrations.

question: Where does the crackle in WASAPI exclusive come from?
statement: The bursts are tied to the device period of the exclusive path: the 3.000 ms (144-sample) burst grid seen in V012 is the driver/device period, and bursts occur when the requested block is not a whole multiple of that period (128 and 256 are not; 144 and 288 are), so blocks that are whole multiples of the period capture clean.
prediction: In WASAPI exclusive 48000 Hz, Lab tone captures at blocks 144 and 288 show a lower burst rate than blocks 128 and 256 (3 captures each, same mount procedure); the grid phase concentration R at P = 144 stays near 1.0 in damaged captures at any block.
refuted_if: Blocks 144 and 288 give the same damaged share as 128 and 256 (all damaged or the same bursts per second within the repeat spread) in at least 3 captures each, or damaged captures at 144 / 288 show no 3.000 ms grid.

question: What is the lowest real round trip per audio path, and can it be 20 ms or less?
statement: In the exclusive-type paths the real round trip falls roughly linearly with the block size down to a floor set by the converters and the driver period, so the lowest real round trip is reached at the smallest block the path runs without dropouts, and the fitted line (RTT = intercept + slope x block time) tells how many block times of buffering the path adds.
prediction: latency_lab per-run median RTT versus block time (frames / 48000) over blocks 64 to 288 is monotone non-decreasing in the exclusive and ASIO4ALL paths with a positive fitted slope and an intercept above 0 ms; RTT never lies below block time.
refuted_if: RTT changes by 1.0 ms or less across the whole sweep 64 to 288 in a path (block size is then not the lever, the driver period decides), or RTT is not monotone beyond the run-to-run spread measured in E006.
